title: Stitches for a wound
what: The doctor cleans the wound and closes it with stitches, staples, or special skin glue. This helps it heal faster and leaves a neater scar.
why: For deep cuts, wounds with gaping edges, or wounds on the face, hands, or joints.
duration: usually 15 to 40 minutes; stitches usually come out after 5 to 14 days, depending on the spot
tell_doctor: How and when you got the wound, and what cut you
When you last had a tetanus shot

prepare.title: Bleeding
prepare.text: Press a clean cloth on the wound and hold it. Raise the arm or leg above heart level.

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: The sooner the better. Doctors usually try to close a wound within the first hours.

prepare.title: Do not
prepare.text: Do not pour alcohol into the wound or put anything on it. You can rinse it with clean water.

bring: Your tetanus shot record, if you have it
steps: The wound is rinsed and cleaned with antiseptic
Numbing injections are given around it
The edges are stitched or held together
You are told when to come for a dressing change and stitch removal
feel: The numbing injections sting for a few seconds
During stitching you feel pulling, but no pain
When the numbing wears off, the wound will ache
after: Keep the bandage dry for the first 1 to 2 days, or as long as your doctor says
Have the stitches removed on time, not earlier and not later
After the stitches are out, protect the scar from the sun
red_flags: Heavy bleeding that does not stop with pressure: call emergency services
The wound becomes red, hot, or has pus, or you get a fever
Numbness, or fingers that do not move well

faq.a: Usually after 5 to 7 days on the face, 7 to 10 days on the body and arms, and longer on the legs and joints. Your doctor will tell you exactly.
Usually a short shower is fine after 1 to 2 days. Then pat the wound dry. Ask your doctor.

reminders.text: Dressing change or stitch removal tomorrow. Keep the bandage dry and bring your ID.
